questions.prompt: The course's CREATE TABLE conventions include which set?
options: utf8mb4 charset · AUTO_INCREMENT ids · ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP for updated_at · ENGINE=InnoDB
utf8 charset · UUID ids · manual updated_at · MyISAM
latin1 · SERIAL ids · triggers for timestamps · MEMORY engine
ascii · GUID ids · no timestamps · CSV engine
questions.explain: **utf8mb4** (real 4-byte Unicode — MySQL's `utf8` is broken 3-byte), **AUTO_INCREMENT** (id returned as lastInsertId/insertId), **ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP** re-stamps updated_at, **InnoDB** = transactional/ACID engine in every course table.

questions.prompt: The three sacred PDO options of the course are:
questions.explain: **ERRMODE_EXCEPTION** (throw PDOException → try/catch works), **FETCH_ASSOC** (assoc arrays, JSON-friendly), **EMULATE_PREPARES=false** (real server-side prepared statements). DSN format: `mysql:host=127.0.0.1;dbname=books_api;charset=utf8mb4`.

questions.prompt: The safe way to fetch a book by user-supplied id:
questions.explain: **Data goes through a placeholder — never into the SQL string.** prepare → execute([$id]) → fetchAll. That separation of code from data is exactly what defeats SQL injection.

questions.prompt: With EMULATE_PREPARES=false, why does `WHERE title LIKE :q OR author LIKE :q` fail?
options: A named placeholder cannot be reused — each must be unique (:q_title, :q_author) or you get SQLSTATE HY093
OR is not allowed in prepared statements
questions.explain: Real prepared statements forbid reusing a named placeholder: use **unique names** (`:q_title`, `:q_author`) and bind both, else **SQLSTATE HY093**. New PK after INSERT: `$pdo->lastInsertId()`; rows affected: `$stmt->rowCount()`.

items: UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 100 WHERE id = 1
UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 100 WHERE id = 2
questions.explain: **beginTransaction** opens the all-or-nothing block → both updates → **commit** makes them permanent; ANY exception → **rollBack** undoes everything. Counting: `SELECT COUNT(*) AS total` then `fetchColumn()` pulls the single scalar.

questions.prompt: After `SELECT COUNT(*) AS total FROM books`, which PDOStatement method pulls the single scalar out? (method name)
questions.explain: **`fetchColumn()`** — returns the first column of the next row; perfect for single-value aggregates.
